subject: Approach to multiple modeling similar lanes

messages.author: 32ca34ebc225cb13
messages.subject: Approach to multiple modeling similar lanes
parts:
I have a problem with an apple pack house that grades the apples based on diameter.  the diameter of the apples is normally distributed with mean around 59mm with a sd of ~5mm.  Once the diameter has been measured (using high speed cameras). the apples are sent to particular packing lanes to be put in tubes.  Multiple packing lanes are needed for the diameter ranges that are in the middle of the bell curve.  The shoulder sizes generally need only one.  We know the capacity of the packing lane and can therefore, a priori, work out how many lanes will be required for each size.  Hitherto only manual packing lanes were employed which all had the same packing rate.  We are now looking at introducing robotic packing lanes, in combination with the manual packing lanes, which have a much greater throughput.

When I simulated the packhouse previously with Simmer I used the branch command to deal with the different sized apples and the capacity of each resource (a particular lane(s) for each fruit size) to deal with multiple lanes.  Now I potentially have both robotic and manual packing lanes on the same sized fruit and from a resource point of view I wondered how I could deal with this? The fruit will be identical but the rate will be the much greater with the robots and the decision as to which lane to send it to will be generally be a function of the shortest queue.

I feel like I could use the Select command with a custom policy but I am unsure how to go about this.

Any help is greatly appreciated

Warm regards
Stuart

Now I potentially have both robotic and manual packing lanes on the same sized fruit and from a resource point of view I wondered how I could deal with this? The fruit will be identical but the rate will be the much greater with the robots and the decision as to which lane to send it to will be generally be a function of the shortest queue.
>

So if I understood correctly, you have a first decision level in which
you send the apples to a subset of packing lines based on the size,
and now you have a second decision level in which you select robot or
human. Then I'd say that select() is a good choice for that second
level. You already have a shortest-queue policy implemented, and if
you have further requirements for the decision, you can always write
your own policy, as you said.

Iñaki
